Hadad (king of Edom)
HAY-dad
proper noun
Hebrew hadad, “mighty” or “fierce” (a name borne also by an Edomite idol), the name of the fourth king of Edom, the son of Bedad, of the city Avith.

📖 Biblical Definition

Hadad the son of Bedad reigned in Edom after the death of Husham (Gen 36:35). He is the fourth king in the line of Esau, and of him alone among these kings is a deed of war recorded: he smote Midian in the field of Moab. The name of his city was Avith. This Hadad was a man of might in his generation, prevailing over Midian upon Moab’s plain, and yet his conquest is set in the same dry catalogue with all the others, for the Holy Ghost will not let the warrior boast: Hadad smote Midian, and Hadad died (Gen 36:36). The name Hadad was borne also by an idol of the Syrians and Edomites, a thing of nought; and so the very names of Esau’s kings carry the savour of the false worship that filled the land. Edom was lifted up in worldly pride and in might, and Edom shall be brought down. The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock (Oba 1:3). Hadad’s sword could subdue Midian, but it could not stay his own death, nor purchase his soul, nor stand against the LORD who weigheth the nations as the small dust of the balance. Here is the lesson of every conqueror of the earth: he prevaileth for an hour and then lieth down, and the kingdom passeth to another. Only the King who conquered death reigneth and dieth no more.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Hadad the son of Bedad, of Avith, the fourth king of Edom, who smote Midian in the field of Moab (Gen 36:35).

expand to see more

HADAD, the son of Bedad, the fourth king who reigned in the land of Edom.

He smote Midian in the field of Moab; the name of his city was Avith (Gen 36:35).

He reigned after the death of Husham of Temani.

His name was borne also by an idol of the Edomites and Syrians.

His conquest and his death are set together in the record of Edom’s kings.

📖 Key Scripture

Gen 36:35 — "And Husham died, and Hadad the son of Bedad, who smote Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his stead: and the name of his city was Avith."

Oba 1:3 — "The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?"

Gen 36:31 — "And these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom, before there reigned any king over the children of Israel."

Heb 12:16 — "Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A king of the genealogical record, not a contested doctrine; Hadad the conqueror witnesses against the worldly pride and might of Edom that the LORD has promised to bring down.

expand to see more

Hadad the son of Bedad is a figure of the sacred register, the fourth king of Edom and the only one of whom a deed of war is told. No movement of the present age has troubled itself to redefine him; the dictionary records him that the reader may know him for a real warrior-king of a real city, Avith, in the land of Esau.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the LORD bringeth down the pride and the might of the nations. Hadad smote Midian, yet Hadad died; his very name was an Edomite idol, a savour of the false worship of Esau’s land. Edom was lifted up and shall be abased: The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee (Oba 1:3). The mightiest conqueror is dust before the King who conquered death.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for “mighty” or “fierce,” Hadad names the fourth king of Edom, of Avith, who smote Midian.

expand to see more

Hadad — Hebrew hadad, “mighty” or “fierce.”

He was the son of Bedad, the fourth king of Edom (Gen 36:35).

He smote Midian in the field of Moab; his city was Avith.

The name was borne also by an idol of the Edomites and Syrians.

He is recorded among the kings of Edom in Genesis and First Chronicles.

Usage

"Hadad smote Midian, yet the next word of him is that he died."

"His name was an Edomite idol, marking the false worship of Esau’s land."

"The mightiest conqueror cannot stay his own death nor stand against the LORD."
